subject: Archaeology
title: Pompeii's Graffiti: Ancient Social Media
description: One-minute skill: Pompeii's Graffiti: Ancient Social Media.

hook.text: Pompeii's walls are covered in over 11,000 pieces of graffiti — love notes, insults, political ads, and bar tabs.

buildup.text: One scrawl reads: 'Gaius was here.' Another says: 'I don't want to sell my husband.' Romans were just like us.

discovery.text: Election slogans cover entire walls. Candidates had their supporters paint endorsements everywhere — ancient billboards.

twist.text: Some graffiti is shockingly crude. Bathroom walls, taverns, and brothels all have messages too rude to translate here.

climax.text: This graffiti is the most honest record of Roman daily life — unfiltered, uncensored, and deeply human.

punchline.text: Romans invented social media. They just wrote it on walls.

quiz.question: Why is Pompeii's graffiti historically valuable?
options: It contains the only surviving examples of the Roman alphabet
It provides an unfiltered, uncensored record of Roman daily life
It reveals secret codes used by Roman military intelligence
